newsitem.title: PERU: 'Cerpa' the dog will get home after Peru siege.
newsitem.headline: 'Cerpa' the dog will get home after Peru siege.

text.p: A stray dog that has become a favourite among journalists camped outside the Japanese ambassador's residence will not be homeless when the current hostage crisis is over, an animal protection group said on Wednesday.

"He is not just the centre of attraction at the moment. He is a living thing," said Maria de Garcia, a member of the Friends of Animals Association. She said the group was looking for a home for the dog, fearing that once the crisis is resolved the animal will be forgotten.

The black and white terrier mix has been dubbed "Cerpa" after the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, who had led the bold attack on the ambassador's residence Dec. 17. The rebels were still holding 74 men hostage on Wednesday.
Cerpa became fond of local and foreign journalists, who have fussed over him and fed him take-out pizza and Japanese food during the month-long crisis.
